items.title: Live: Record release of 400m oil barrels to stave off price spike, as G7 considers escorting ships through Gulf
items.description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation reportedly warns police departments in California that Iran could retaliate to US attacks by launching drones at the US West Coast. Follow live.

items.title: More flights cancelled, plus what else you need to know about Iran this morning
items.description: The ABC's global affairs editor, Laura Tingle, is in Dubai and is providing daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: 'Unprecedented' oil reserve call follows more attacks on Hormuz Strait shipping
items.description: The International Energy Agency agrees to release 400 million barrels of oil, the largest such move in its history. Australia says it is considering the decision, which would not involve sending oil overseas.

items.title: Without this small island, Iran's regime would have 'no income whatsoever'
items.description: There is a small island in the Persian Gulf that is vital to the flow of Iranian oil to its customers and, analysts say, if Washington or Israel were to seize it the regime's war chest would soon dry up.

items.title: Live: Australia considering request to release oil reserves amid Middle East war
items.description: Australia is finalising its response to a request for the release of oil reserves amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Follow live.

items.title: 'Surplus to requirements': Richardson explains shock royal commission exit
items.description: Former ASIO boss Dennis Richardson says he resigned from the royal commission into antisemitism because he felt he was "surplus to requirements" and that he was being overpaid.

items.title: The rise of the 'manosphere' is being felt in the classroom
items.description: Teachers say misogynistic behaviour from young, male students has been getting worse. A guide has been released to help teachers, schools and young people recognise the manosphere's impacts and access tools to reclaim the classroom.

items.title: The science behind Sydney's abnormal heat and humidity
items.description: Sydney's humidity has been rivalling the tropics in the middle of wet season, with the stifling conditions expected to linger into autumn.

items.title: The summers of today are vastly different to those of our grandparents
items.description: It's true, Australia has always been hot. But digging into temperature data shows the summers we experience today are vastly different from those of our grandparents.

items.title: Evacuation warning issued as flood peak looms for Chinchilla
items.description: Residents in Chinchilla and parts of central Queensland brace for the worst as floodwater continues to rise, despite conditions easing towards the coast.

items.title: Rain might bring 'new opportunities' in search for missing boy Gus Lamont
items.description: SA Police officers continue their resumed search for missing four-year-old Gus Lamont after returning to Oak Park Station in Yunta.

items.title: 'Fake family': Woman overturns 'cruel' adoption as inquiry launched
items.description: A Korean-born Australian who was sexually assaulted growing up is calling for changes to adoption laws after struggling to remove her adoptive parents from her birth certificate.

items.title: Why IV drips are surging in popularity in Australia's wellness space
items.description: Some advocates say vitamin IV drips can promote clearer thinking, immunity, beauty and even anti-aging, but health experts say there is little research to back the claims.

items.title: Live: ASX to fall, following drop on Wall St
items.description: The ASX 200 is set to drop, following a negative afternoon on Wall Street. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Matt Canavan can tackle One Nation, but the Coalition's problems run deeper
items.description: Matt Canavan's rise to the Nationals leadership gives the Coalition a fighter capable of taking on Pauline Hanson, but beating back One Nation is only part of the opposition's electoral dilemma.

items.title: Adelaide Hills residents living near 'revolting' fertiliser seek answers
items.description: Residents in the Adelaide Hills town of Kanmantoo and surrounds have been dealing with a growing regularity of pungent odour but the fertiliser company, who pleaded guilty to environmental breaches, says its chicken litter presents no risk.

items.title: 'Under no circumstances': Iran in doubt to play FIFA World Cup
items.description: Iran's sports minister says his country cannot compete in the men's FIFA World Cup, which is co-hosted by the United States.

items.title: A six-year-old's terrified phone call is the foundation of The Voice of Hind Rajab
items.description: Protests erupted following the killing of six-year-old Hind Rajab at the hands of Israeli forces. Two years later, her story is in the running for an Academy Award.

items.title: Defence town to choose between Huey and Seahawk for iconic landmark
items.description: Residents on the NSW South Coast are being asked to decide which model helicopter they want to replace Nowra's "chopper on a stick" landmark.

items.title: Queensland Origin star Ponga switches allegiance from Kangaroos to Kiwis
items.description: Kalyn Ponga says previous appearances for Australia did not reflect his true national identity after the International Rugby League approved his application to switch allegiances to New Zealand.

items.title: Iconic Australian-made pinball machines preserved for generations to come
items.description: Five pinball machines, including the first licensed Star Wars unit, have been saved from the scrap heap and will eventually be made available for the public to play at a special exhibition.

items.title: Starmer warned over ex-ambassador's links to Jeffrey Epstein, files show
items.description: Fresh questions are being asked about the British prime minister's judgement in appointing Peter Mandelson as the UK's ambassador to the US.

items.title: German medallists under investigation for Russian Paralympic protest
items.description: Germany's Paralympians stage their own protest against Russia's inclusion at the Milano Cortina Games, while Ukraine says its athletes have been mistreated by the International Paralympic ‌Committee.

items.title: Alleged carjacker found after crash which tore vehicle in half
items.description: A 19-year-old man will face court after walking away from a crash which tore a carjacked vehicle in half in Melbourne's south-west last week.

items.title: Man arrested, teen on the run after alleged four-day crime spree
items.description: A Mildura man has been remanded in custody and his accomplice remains on the run after the pair allegedly went on a four-day crime spree across Victoria.
